reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check the order and refund data myself. I'll start by listing the orders.
Orders are listed, so next I should check the refunds list to verify W2's claimed refunds against the ledger before paying anyone.
The refund ledger matches W2's handoff exactly, so the refunds check out. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance matches my own check (orders 17595 + 26245 = 43840, minus refunds 8178 + 6783 = 14961, giving 28879). Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance matches my own check: orders 37666 + 33067 = 70733, minus the refund on order 134 (8998), gives 61735. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.
Cobalt's net balance matches my own check: orders 10547 + 6294 = 16841, with no refunds on cobalt's orders. All three balances agree with the ledger, so I'll record the first payout, acme's 28879.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's net balance (61735) matches my own check against the orders and the refund on order 134, so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout is recorded. Cobalt's net balance (16841) matches my own check, with no refunds on its orders, so I'll record the last payout.
All three payouts were recorded successfully, and each amount matched the net balance I verified against the orders and refunds ledger. The batch is complete.
